q: A wait-for graph is used to detect deadlock when:
options: each resource type has only one instance
exp: A wait-for graph is obtained from the resource-allocation graph by removing resource nodes and works for single instances.

q: A user program requests a kernel service by executing a:
exp: A system call is invoked through a trap, which switches the CPU to kernel mode and runs the handler.

q: A process arrives at time 4, has a CPU burst of 6 ms and completes at time 20 (waiting only in the ready queue). What is its waiting time?
exp: Turnaround = 20 - 4 = 16; waiting = turnaround - burst = 16 - 6 = 10.

q: Thrashing occurs in a virtual memory system when:
options: the CPU is idle because no process is ready
a process spends more time paging than executing
exp: Excessive page faults, often from too high a degree of multiprogramming, cause thrashing.

q: The main purpose of journaling in file systems such as ext4 and NTFS is to:
options: keep the file system consistent and speed up recovery after a crash
exp: Changes are logged before being applied, so after a crash the log can be replayed to restore consistency.

q: Which page replacement algorithm is free from Belady's anomaly?
exp: LRU and Optimal are stack algorithms; the set of pages in n frames is always a subset of that in n+1 frames.

q: The degree of multiprogramming is controlled by the:
exp: The long-term (job) scheduler decides how many processes are admitted into memory.

q: A known drawback of SSTF disk scheduling is:
options: starvation of requests far from the current head position
it needs the disk to be empty
it cannot handle more than 8 requests
exp: New requests near the head may keep arriving and delay distant requests indefinitely.

q: The primary role of an operating system is to:
options: translate high-level programs into machine code
act as a resource manager and provide an interface between user and hardware
create hardware drivers only for printers
store data permanently on the disk
exp: The OS allocates CPU, memory and I/O devices and offers services to users and applications.

q: The starting address of the Interrupt Service Routine is obtained from the:
exp: The interrupt number indexes the vector table, which holds ISR addresses.

q: A race condition occurs when:
options: two processes have the same priority
the outcome depends on the order in which concurrent processes access shared data
a process runs faster than another
exp: Unsynchronized access to shared data makes results depend on scheduling interleaving.

q: In a Linux system, user and system configuration files are generally stored in the directory:
exp: /etc holds configuration files such as passwd and hosts; /dev has device files and /proc is a virtual process file system.

q: Which statement distinguishes livelock from deadlock?
options: Livelock requires a minimum of four processes
In livelock, processes keep changing state but make no progress
Livelock occurs only in single-processor systems
In livelock, processes are blocked forever without any activity
exp: Livelocked processes are not blocked; they actively respond to each other yet never finish.

q: Which statement about a multilevel feedback queue scheduler is correct?
options: It cannot use Round Robin in any queue
It requires prior knowledge of exact burst times
Processes can move between queues, which also helps prevent starvation
Processes are permanently assigned to one queue
exp: MLFQ promotes and demotes processes among queues based on behaviour and waiting time, so aging can prevent starvation.

q: In the buddy system, a request for 70 KB is made from a 256 KB free block. What is the internal fragmentation in the block allocated to it?
exp: The 256 KB block is split into 128 KB buddies; 128 KB is allocated, wasting 128 - 70 = 58 KB.

q: Match the file systems with their typical operating systems: (i) ext4 (ii) NTFS (iii) APFS. Which mapping is correct?
exp: ext4 is the common Linux file system, NTFS is Windows, APFS is Apple's file system for macOS and iOS.

q: The Linux kernel is classified as:
options: a monolithic kernel with loadable modules
exp: Linux runs most services in kernel space but supports dynamically loadable modules.

q: The Optimal page replacement algorithm is not practical because it:
options: needs knowledge of future page references
exp: It replaces the page that will not be used for the longest time, which cannot be known in advance; it serves as a benchmark.

q: In the many-to-one multithreading model, which is a major drawback?
options: Thread creation requires a kernel call
Each user thread needs a kernel thread
If one thread makes a blocking system call, the entire process blocks
exp: All user threads map to one kernel thread, so a blocking call blocks all of them and there is no parallelism on multiprocessors.

q: The time taken by the dispatcher to stop one process and start another running is called:
exp: Dispatch latency is the time for the dispatcher to perform the context switch and resume a process.

q: C-SCAN is preferred over SCAN because it:
options: provides a more uniform waiting time
exp: C-SCAN services requests in one direction and returns quickly, so cylinders at either end are treated more fairly.

q: Embedded operating systems are typically characterized by:
options: small memory footprint and a fixed dedicated function
exp: They are designed for devices such as appliances and controllers with limited resources.

q: Priority inversion happens when:
options: a high-priority process waits for a lock held by a low-priority process that is preempted by a medium-priority process
a low-priority process always runs before higher ones
priorities are assigned in decreasing order
exp: The medium-priority process indirectly delays the high-priority one; priority inheritance is the usual fix.

q: Which command displays a dynamic, continuously updated view of running processes and CPU/memory usage?
exp: top refreshes periodically, while ps gives a one-time snapshot.

q: Which of the following is NOT a method of recovering from deadlock?
options: Aborting processes one at a time until the cycle is broken
Increasing the time quantum of the CPU scheduler
exp: Recovery uses process termination or resource preemption; changing the quantum has no effect on the deadlock.

q: In two-level paging with a 32-bit address, 12-bit offset and a 10-bit outer-page index, how many bits index the inner page table?
In the counting method of free-space management, each free-list entry contains:
options: the address of the first free block and the number of contiguous free blocks following it
the size of the entire disk
only the address of the next free block
exp: Counting exploits the fact that free blocks often occur in contiguous runs.

q: Response time in CPU scheduling is the time:
options: a process spends waiting in the ready queue in total
from submission until the process completes
a process spends executing on the CPU
from submission of a request until the first response is produced
exp: Response time measures how soon the first output is produced, important for interactive systems.

q: A device driver is best described as:
options: an application used to install programs
kernel-level software that lets the OS communicate with a hardware device controller
a hardware component inside the disk
a type of CPU scheduling policy
exp: Device drivers provide a uniform interface between the OS and the device-specific hardware.

q: During system start-up, the bootstrap loader (boot loader) is responsible for:
options: locating and loading the operating system kernel into main memory
exp: After firmware (BIOS/UEFI) tests the hardware, the boot loader loads the kernel and passes control to it.

q: The second-chance (clock) page replacement algorithm makes use of:
options: a reference bit for each page
exp: A page with reference bit 1 gets a second chance (bit cleared), otherwise it is replaced.

q: When a parent process terminates before its child, the child process is adopted by:
options: the shell that started the parent
exp: Orphaned children are re-parented to init/systemd (PID 1), which reaps them on exit.

q: Seek time of a disk is the time required to:
options: move the read/write head to the desired cylinder
rotate the desired sector under the head
exp: Seek time is the head-positioning time; rotational latency and transfer time are separate.

q:
Assertion (A): Time-sharing systems provide good interactive response.
Reason (R): The CPU is switched among users after a small time quantum.
Which option is correct?
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
exp: Rapid switching with a small quantum gives each user quick turns on the CPU, which explains the good response.

q: A counting semaphore is initialised to 2. Five processes each execute a P (wait) operation and none executes V. How many processes are blocked?
exp: The first two P operations succeed (value 0); the remaining three block.

q: The command df -h is used to:
options: display the size of a particular file only
display disk space usage of mounted file systems in human-readable form
exp: df reports free and used space on file systems; -h prints sizes in K, M, G.

q: In the Banker's algorithm, if Max for a process is (7, 5, 3) and its current Allocation is (0, 1, 0), what is its Need vector?
exp: Need = Max - Allocation = (7-0, 5-1, 3-0) = (7, 4, 3).

q: Demand paging works efficiently mainly because of:
exp: Programs tend to access a small set of pages repeatedly, so few page faults occur.

q: In Unix, the three standard file descriptors 0, 1 and 2 correspond to:
exp: By convention 0 is standard input, 1 standard output, 2 standard error.

q: SJF scheduling predicts the next CPU burst by exponential averaging: τ(n+1) = α·t(n) + (1-α)·τ(n). If α = 0.5, the initial prediction τ0 = 10 ms and the first actual burst t0 = 6 ms, what is the next prediction τ1?
